findings.title: Saved-all feedback in generator desyncs from actual bank state (dedup silently drops re-saves)
findings.problem: save(_:) calls bank.add(...) (whose @discardableResult Bool reports whether it was actually inserted) but ignores the return value and unconditionally marks the question Saved via savedIDs.insert. WorkbookQuestionBankStore.add dedups by lowercased prompt+answer, so if the generator produces a question whose prompt+answer already exists in the bank (very common when regenerating with the same source/instructions), add() returns false and nothing is stored, yet the card flips to '已保存 · Saved' and the Save button disables. The learner believes a question was saved into the bank when it was not. Same applies to 'Save all'.
findings.fix: Capture the boolean: let didInsert = bank.add(...). Only insert into savedIDs when didInsert is true, or (better) treat an existing duplicate as already-saved by marking it Saved while surfacing nothing misleading. Mirror the grading view's isInBank() content-match approach so the Saved badge reflects bank membership, not just a tap.

findings.title: Generator 'Saved' state is keyed on GeneratedReviewQuestion.id which is regenerated each decode, so it cannot survive a Regenerate and is purely per-render UUID
findings.problem: GeneratedReviewQuestion.id is `let id = UUID()` assigned at decode time (AIWordExplanationService.swift:1376). On Regenerate, generate() replaces `generated` and clears savedIDs/revealed, which is correct. However there is no persistence of which generated items were already added to the bank across a regenerate; combined with the dedup-driven add described above, a learner who saves a question, regenerates, and gets a textually identical question will see it as un-saved and tapping Save is a silent no-op (add() returns false). This compounds finding #1's confusion.
findings.fix: After loading bank, pre-populate savedIDs for any freshly generated question whose dedup key already exists in bank.questions (e.g. via bank.contains(WorkbookQuestion(generated: q))), so already-banked items render as Saved and the Save button correctly reflects reality.

findings.title: Detail view 'Add all to Review Bank' gives no partial-success feedback and re-tap is impossible after first add
findings.problem: The button loops `for question in session.questions { _ = bank.add(question) }` discarding each Bool, then sets addedAll = true and disables itself permanently for the lifetime of the view. If some questions were already in the bank (e.g. they were added from the live grading screen via 'Add to Bank'), the button still claims '已加入题库 · Added to Bank' even though it may have added zero new items. It also cannot reflect bank membership when the detail is first opened (always shows the un-added label even if everything is already banked), which is inconsistent with the live grading screen that uses content-based isInBank().
findings.fix: Initialize addedAll by checking bank membership on appear (e.g. session.questions.allSatisfy { bank.contains($0) }), and/or count actual insertions from add()'s return to show 'Added N' vs already present. Keep the button enabled when not all questions are banked.

findings.title: Redundant local rebinding of imageID inside .task(id:) is dead code (harmless but misleading)
findings.problem: Inside `.task(id: imageID)` the closure does `let id = imageID` then uses `id`. The comment-implied intent (snapshotting to avoid capturing self/changing state) is unnecessary: imageID is a `let` stored property of a value-type view, already immutable and safely captured. The local alias adds noise and can mislead a future reader into thinking there is a capture hazard being defended against. The async load itself is correct: file IO runs in Task.detached off the main actor and the resulting value-type Image is assigned back on the MainActor-isolated view, which is sound.
findings.fix: Remove the `let id = imageID` line and use imageID directly, or leave as-is; this is style-only with no runtime effect.

findings.title: Re-tapping Grade double-counts stats and duplicates history sessions + on-disk images
findings.location: grade() lines 571-619; canGrade lines 65-67; gradeButton line 373
findings.problem: After a successful grade, `isGrading` returns to false while `workbookImages`/`answerImages` remain populated, so `canGrade` is true and the Grade button is re-enabled. Each subsequent tap of Grade unconditionally: (1) calls `LearningActivityStore.shared.recordQuestionsGraded(graded.questions.count)`, inflating today's questionsGraded streak/stat by the full count again; (2) calls `WorkbookGradingHistoryStore.shared.add(session)`, which inserts without any dedup (WorkbookBank.swift add() lines 318-321), producing duplicate history entries for the same workbook; and (3) re-runs `WorkbookImageStore.saveAll(...)` which writes a fresh copy of every scanned photo to Application Support under new UUIDs. So grading the same images twice triple-pollutes: stats, history list, and disk usage. The most likely real-world trigger is a user who re-grades after tweaking custom instructions, or who taps Grade again to 'retry' — all of which the UI permits. None of this existed in HEAD (recordQuestionsGraded, history persistence and image save are all new this session).
findings.fix: Make re-grade idempotent or block it. Options: track a per-input signature (e.g. hash of wbImages+ansImages+custom) and skip session/stat/image persistence when it matches the last graded signature; or reset inputs after a successful grade; or gate the persistence block behind a `!didSaveSession || inputsChanged` check. At minimum, only call recordQuestionsGraded / history.add / saveAll once per distinct input set. Clearing `didSaveSession` and re-counting on every tap is the core defect.

findings.title: Camera capture downscales a full-resolution photo synchronously on the main actor
findings.problem: CameraImagePicker delivers `info[.originalImage]` (the full-resolution camera frame, often 12MP / several MB) as JPEG via its delegate, which fires on the main thread. The `.fullScreenCover` onCapture closure calls `addCapturedImage`, which runs `downscaledJPEG(data)` — a synchronous CGImageSource thumbnail + JPEG re-encode — directly on the MainActor before appending. Every other ingestion path (Photos via `loadDownscaled`, Files via `loadDownscaledFiles`, drag-drop via the Task in handleDrop) performs the same downscale OFF the main actor in an async/static context. So the camera path uniquely blocks the UI for the duration of the decode/encode (tens of ms+, larger on older devices), and does it while the full-screen cover is dismissing — a visible hitch.
findings.fix: Move the downscale off the main actor for the camera path too, mirroring the other ingestion methods. E.g. make addCapturedImage async/Task-based: `Task { let processed = await Task.detached { downscaledJPEG(data) }.value; await MainActor.run { append } }`, or route camera bytes through the same `loadDownscaled`-style off-main helper.

findings.title: "Add to Bank" button reports success even when nothing was added (empty-key questions)
findings.location: addToBank lines 629-632; addAllToBank lines 634-640; isInBank lines 625-627
findings.problem: `bank.add(...)` returns false and stores nothing when the dedup key is empty — and the key is `question + "∣" + correctAnswer` lowercased/trimmed (WorkbookBank.swift dedupKey lines 228-232, guarded in add() line 185). A graded question whose `question` and `correctAnswer` are both empty (tolerant decode defaults them to "") therefore never enters the bank. But addToBank ignores the return value (`_ = bank.add(...)`) and unconditionally does `savedToBankIDs.insert(question.id)`, so isInBank() then returns true and the card shows '已在题库 · In Bank' (disabled). The user is told the question was banked when it silently wasn't, and it will be absent from WorkbookQuestionBankView. Low impact because such fully-empty questions are rare, but the UI state is dishonest.
findings.fix: Only mark as banked when the add (or pre-existing membership) is real: `if bank.add(WorkbookQuestion(graded: question)) || bank.containsGraded(question) { savedToBankIDs.insert(question.id) }`. Apply the same in addAllToBank so the bulk button doesn't mark un-addable questions as in-bank.

findings.title: "Add all to Review Bank" bulk button gives no added-state feedback and stays active
findings.location: resultsSection bulk button lines 442-450; addAllToBank lines 634-640
findings.problem: Unlike the per-question card (which flips to '已在题库' and disables) and unlike the analogous GradedSessionDetailView.addToBankButton (which tracks `addedAll` and disables), the '全部加入题库 · Add all to Review Bank' button here never reflects that it was pressed and never disables. Repeated taps are safe due to bank dedup, but the user gets no confirmation the action took effect, which is inconsistent with the rest of the feature's UX and may prompt repeated tapping. Not data loss, purely a state/feedback gap.
findings.fix: Add an `@State private var didAddAllToBank = false`, set it in addAllToBank(), and reflect it on the label/disabled state (e.g. show '已全部加入 · Added all' and `.disabled(didAddAllToBank)`), resetting it alongside savedToBankIDs at the start of grade().

findings.title: Re-grading the same loaded photos creates a duplicate session, re-saves the images to disk, and double-counts questionsGraded
findings.problem: After a successful grade(), `isGrading` is reset to false but `workbookImages`/`answerImages` are NOT cleared, so `canGrade` becomes true again and the Grade button is re-enabled while the same photos are still loaded. Tapping Grade a second time runs the full path again: WorkbookImageStore.saveAll() writes a SECOND copy of the identical scans to Application Support under fresh UUIDs, WorkbookGradingHistoryStore.shared.add() inserts a SECOND GradedSession for the same workbook, and LearningActivityStore.shared.recordQuestionsGraded(graded.questions.count) is called again — inflating today's questionsGraded (and thus activityScore/heatmap) by the question count on every extra tap. Unlike the review-bank add() which dedups on prompt+answer, GradedSession.add() and recordQuestionsGraded() have no idempotency guard. This is a regression introduced by wiring the new persistence (image store + history + activity counter) into a button that stays live after the first run.
findings.fix: Make re-grade idempotent or block it. Simplest: guard at the top of the save block so a session/activity is only recorded once per input set — e.g. clear `workbookImages`/`answerImages` (or set a `didSaveSession`-style latch into canGrade) after a successful grade, or skip the history.add()+recordQuestionsGraded() when `didSaveSession` is already true for the current images. If intentional re-grading is desired, delete the previous session's images (WorkbookImageStore.deleteAll) and remove its session before adding the new one so disk usage and the counter don't accumulate.

findings.title: WorkbookImageStore.saveAll partial failure silently drops scans from the saved session with no caller feedback
findings.location: WorkbookImageStore.saveAll (lines 397-399) / save (lines 385-394); consumed in WorkbookGradingView.grade() lines 591-604
findings.problem: saveAll uses `datas.compactMap { save($0) }`, so any image whose `data.write` throws (disk full, sandbox/protected-data unavailable while device locked, etc.) is silently omitted from the returned ID array. The GradedSession is then persisted with fewer workbookImageIDs/answerImageIDs than the user actually scanned, and the only trace is an os_log line. The user sees a saved history entry that is missing some of their original photos with no warning. Image IDs and the source `datas` are also positionally decoupled, so there's no way to tell which page was lost.
findings.fix: Have grade() compare returned ID counts against input counts (wbIDs.count == wbImages.count, ansIDs.count == ansImages.count) and surface a non-fatal warning (e.g. set errorMessage or a banner) when some scans failed to persist, so the user knows the history entry is incomplete. Optionally make save throwing so callers can react per-image.

findings.title: DailyActivity tolerant decode can desync the internal dateKey from its dictionary key when dateKey is missing/corrupt
findings.problem: `dateKey` is a `let` and on decode failure falls back to today's key: `(try? c.decode(String.self, forKey: .dateKey)) ?? DailyActivity.keyFormatter.string(from: Date())`. The store holds activities as `[String: DailyActivity]` keyed by the JSON object key, which is independent of the decoded `dateKey` field. If a stored entry's `dateKey` value were ever absent/garbled, that entry would keep its real map key (e.g. "2025-01-01") but its internal `dateKey` (used by `date`, `id`, and the heatmap cell's displayed date) would become today — silently mislabeling a historical day's data. In normal operation dateKey is always present so this rarely fires, and the previous synthesized decoder would have thrown instead (arguably worse), so this is a latent edge case rather than a live bug.
findings.fix: Prefer a sentinel that is obviously invalid over today's date (e.g. fall back to empty string and let `activity.date` resolve via the existing `?? Date()` path), or — since the dictionary key is authoritative — re-derive/repair `dateKey` from the map key after load in LearningActivityStore.loadActivities() so the field can never disagree with its key.

findings.title: Re-grading the same workbook duplicates history, double-counts activity, and orphans/duplicates photos on disk
findings.location: grade() (lines ~571-619) together with canGrade (lines 65-67) and gradeButton (lines 363-374)
findings.problem: grade() unconditionally persists a new GradedSession (with a fresh WorkbookImageStore.saveAll copy of every photo), inserts it into WorkbookGradingHistoryStore, and calls LearningActivityStore.recordQuestionsGraded(...) every time it runs. But canGrade only requires (images present) && (provider) && !isGrading — it does NOT become false once a result exists. After the first grade, the Grade button stays enabled with the same loaded images. Tapping 开始批改 again (or tapping it twice, or re-grading after a tweak to custom instructions) writes a SECOND history session, saves a SECOND on-disk copy of the identical photos (WorkbookImageStore.save generates a new UUID filename each call, so nothing is de-duplicated or overwritten), and adds the question count to today's questionsGraded AGAIN. Result: duplicated grading-history rows, permanently inflated 'Questions Graded' stat and heatmap intensity, and unbounded Application Support disk growth (orphaned image copies are only deletable by removing the now-duplicated history sessions). This is a data-integrity + storage-leak regression introduced by this session's history/persistence wiring.
findings.fix: Make re-grading idempotent. Simplest: when starting a grade after a prior result for the same inputs, delete the previous session's images and remove its history row before saving the new one, or skip persistence entirely if inputs are unchanged. Concretely, track the last-saved session id in @State; at the top of grade() (where result/savedToBankIDs/didSaveSession are reset) also call WorkbookGradingHistoryStore.shared.remove(previousSession) (which deletes its images) and decrement/replace the activity count, then store the new session id. Alternatively disable the Grade button once result != nil (gate canGrade on result == nil) and require an explicit '重新批改 · Re-grade' that first clears the prior session. Without one of these, every extra tap leaks images and corrupts stats.

findings.title: Heatmap selected-date detail row now overcrowded; date/labels clip on narrow iPhones
findings.problem: A fourth Label (questionsGraded) was added to a single non-wrapping HStack that already held wordsLearned + reviewsCompleted + translationsMade, plus a Spacer and a trailing formatted date. HStack spacing was reduced 20 -> 16 to compensate, but there is no minimumScaleFactor / lineLimit / fixedSize handling. On compact-width devices (iPhone SE/mini) with multi-digit counts and a long localized date (.date style), the row can compress the labels' SF Symbols/numbers and squeeze or clip the trailing date. This is purely a layout regression from adding the 4th metric and does not affect data.
findings.fix: Reduce pressure on the row: e.g. apply .layoutPriority/.fixedSize(horizontal: true, vertical: false) to the date Text and/or wrap the four metric Labels in a ViewThatFits or allow the date to drop to .caption2 with .minimumScaleFactor(0.8). A robust option is to move the date above the metrics (VStack) or shorten it to .numeric so four metrics + date always fit on small screens.

# EXECPLAN2 — SwiftMandarin Audit & Feature Implementation

**Generated:** 2026-06-15 · **Branch:** jun-12-2026-ios17-compat

This document has two parts:
- **Part A** — the features implemented this session (camera capture, question bank, review-question generation, grading history, analytics integration, More-tab declutter), with verification status.
- **Part B** — a full audit of the codebase for blocks, bottlenecks, errors, and bugs, produced by a 43-agent parallel workflow (13 subsystem finders → adversarial verification → synthesis), plus architecture & workflow recommendations to make the app more powerful, robust, intuitive, and streamlined.

> Audit scale: **132 findings** (29 high · 54 medium · 49 low), **23 adversarially confirmed** high-severity, **6 refuted**, **86 improvement suggestions**.

---

## Part A — Implemented This Session

All new workbook features are kept inside the **Photo tab** (entry points live in its toolbar menu under a *Workbook* section). Both platforms build clean: `xcodebuild` macOS Debug ✅ and iOS-Simulator Debug ✅, zero errors.

### A1. Direct camera capture for workbook grading
- New `Views/Components/CameraImagePicker.swift` — a `UIImagePickerController(.camera)` wrapper returning JPEG `Data`; iOS-only, macOS stub.
- `WorkbookGradingView` upload sections gained a prominent **拍照 · Camera** button (alongside Photos/Files), shown only when a camera is available (`cameraAction(for:)` returns `nil` on macOS/Simulator/camera-less devices so the button is hidden). Captured photos are downscaled via the existing `downscaledJPEG` path.

### A2. Review-question database (the 'bank')
- New `Models/WorkbookBank.swift`: `WorkbookQuestion` (Codable, tolerant `init(from:)`), `WorkbookQuestionBankStore` (`@Observable @MainActor` singleton over `PersistentCodableStore`, content-dedup, newest-first).
- New `Views/WorkbookQuestionBankView.swift`: browse/filter (All · Workbook · Generated), read-aloud, swipe-delete, clear-all.
- In `WorkbookGradingView`, each graded question has **加入题库 · Add to Bank** and the results have **全部加入题库 · Add all to Review Bank**.

### A3. Generate new review questions from the bank
- New `AIWordExplanationService.generateReviewQuestions(from:count:customInstructions:)` → `[GeneratedReviewQuestion]` (native/learning-language aware; prioritizes wrong/vocab items; tolerant JSON + repair retry; works on Apple Intelligence / Ollama / cloud).
- `ReviewQuestionGeneratorView` (in the bank view): question-count stepper, optional subject tag + custom instructions, generated cards with reveal-answer, read-aloud, and save-to-bank (single + all).

### A4. Grading history with the original scanned photos
- `Models/WorkbookBank.swift` adds `GradedSession` (Codable, tolerant) + `WorkbookGradingHistoryStore`, plus `WorkbookImageStore` — a **file-backed** image store under Application Support (images are far too large for the UserDefaults JSON stores; only file IDs are persisted in JSON; deleting a session deletes its photos).
- New `Views/WorkbookGradingHistoryView.swift`: session list (score ring, date, photo count) → `GradedSessionDetailView` (score, summary, original photos with full-screen viewer, read-only graded cards, add-all-to-bank).
- Each successful grade **auto-saves** a session (off-main image IO via a detached task).

### A5. Analytics / GitHub-style heatmap integration
- `DailyActivity` gains `questionsGraded` with a **tolerant `init(from:)`** so older saved heatmap data still decodes (directly mitigates audit issue #1). `activityScore` now includes graded questions, so the contribution chart reflects them.
- `LearningActivityStore.recordQuestionsGraded(_:)` + `totalQuestionsGraded`; the grader records the day's graded-question count.
- `StatsView`: per-day heatmap detail shows a graded-questions count; Overview grid gains a **Questions Graded** tile.

Removed the **redundant** in-More `HistoryView`/`HistoryRow` (the History tab is canonical) — this also resolves audit quick-win #4.

- New workbook UI uses the established bilingual-literal convention (`中文 · English`). Added 4 catalog keys with `zh-Hans` (`Questions Graded`, `Display & Pinyin`, `Quick Setup`, `About & Support`); catalog re-validated as JSON (625 keys).

---

## Part B — Audit: Bugs, Bottlenecks & Issues

### Executive summary

SwiftMandarin is a feature-rich, ambitious SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app whose breadth (8 tabs, 10-provider AI abstraction, on-device + cloud translation, photo OCR, screenshot stitching, workbook grading, spaced repetition, bilingual UI) outpaces the robustness of its foundations. The codebase is functional but carries three structural risks that should be treated as release-blockers. (1) PERSISTENCE FRAGILITY: every persisted model uses synthesized Codable with no CodingKeys, no schemaVersion, and no defaulting (confirmed by grep across Models/). The PersistentCodableStore .backup is the SAME schema, so any future non-optional field throws keyNotFound on BOTH decode paths and silently wipes all user vocabulary/progress/history on update. Collection decode is all-or-nothing, so one corrupt row drops the whole array. This is the single highest-leverage area to harden. (2) CORRECTNESS BUGS IN CORE FLOWS: the History store records the UI-toggle direction instead of the actually-translated direction (confirmed TranslateView.swift:889 vs :959/:975), corrupting every cross-direction entry and everything derived from it; the audio pipeline spawns a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordering), and the sample-rate converter re-feeds the same buffer forever; screenshot stitching mixes a padded source stride with an unpadded render buffer, corrupting overlap detection; CSV round-trip is lossy for any multi-line field. (3) IA/DISCOVERABILITY DEBT: on the now-live iOS 17 path the legacy TabView emits 8 tabs with no compact-width gating (confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179), so tabs 5-8 — including the app's OWN More tab — collapse under the system More overflow, a confusing collision. The genuinely valuable workbook-grading feature is reachable through exactly one buried sheet (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and nothing else. The More tab is a 601-line catch-all with a duplicate divergent History screen, dead settings, a placeholder App Store ID, and a privacy link pointing at apple.com. Strategically, the app is one solid refactor of the data layer, the information architecture, and a unified translation/learning-direction model away from being genuinely excellent. Concurrency safety is also unverified by the compiler (SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset), masking the audio races. Recommend: freeze new features, ship the persistence envelope + the history-direction fix + the audio-buffer fix first, then execute the IA consolidation (5 tabs + real More hub) and a single source-of-truth learning-direction model.

### Top prioritized issues

**B1. [CRITICAL] Schema evolution will silently wipe all user data on the next model change**  
- *Why:* All persisted models (SavedTerm, CardProgress, DailyActivity, history) use synthesized Codable with no schemaVersion/CodingKeys/decode defaults (verified: grep finds none in Models/). PersistentCodableStore.load decodes the whole collection at once and the .backup is the same schema, so adding any non-optional stored property throws keyNotFound on BOTH the primary and backup decode, and load() returns nil — every saved word, flashcard, streak, and history entry is dropped on update. One corrupt element also discards the entire array.  
- *Fix:* Introduce a versioned envelope {schemaVersion:Int, data:T} in save/load. Decode tolerantly: give new fields explicit decodeIfPresent defaults via custom init(from:), and add a per-element resilient decoder (decode [FailableDecodable<Element>], keep successes, log/drop only the truly-corrupt rows). Ship this BEFORE any further model changes so existing 0.x payloads survive the upgrade.

**B2. [HIGH] History records the UI-toggle direction, not the translated direction — corrupts every cross-direction entry**  
- *Why:* Confirmed: triggerTranslation computes actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection from input content (TranslateView.swift:889), but performTranslation (line 959) and triggerAITranslation (line 923) snapshot directionSnapshot = sharedState.direction (the UI toggle) and write THAT into handleCompletedTranslation (line 975). When the toggle says EN→中 but the user types Chinese, the engine correctly returns English yet history stores direction=englishToChinese. TranslationHistoryEntry.chineseText/.englishText key off direction, so source and target are mislabeled through History, restore, and any term saved from a restored entry.  
- *Fix:* Thread the detected direction through: compute actualDirection = detectedTranslationDirection in performTranslation/triggerAITranslation and pass that (not sharedState.direction) to both the guard comparison and handleCompletedTranslation's direction: argument. Keep the source-text snapshot guard.

**B3. [HIGH] Audio tap captures a non-Sendable AVAudioPCMBuffer into a per-buffer Task (use-after-free + reordered/garbled audio)**  
- *Why:* SpeechRecognitionService.swift:440-446 spawns Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) } per tap callback. AVAudioEngine reclaims that buffer once the closure returns, so the async read touches recycled memory; tens of unstructured Tasks/sec hop to the MainActor with no FIFO guarantee (frames reorder), and in-flight Tasks outlive stop()/removeTap, yielding into a finished continuation. Separately the sample-rate converter input block (lines 473-476) always returns the same buffer with .haveData, so the converter can loop/duplicate frames and never signals end-of-stream.  
- *Fix:* Do conversion synchronously inside the tap and call inputContinuation?.yield(...) directly (the continuation is Sendable/thread-safe); never spawn a Task per buffer. If a hop is unavoidable, deep-copy the buffer first. In the converter block return .haveData once per input chunk then .noDataNow, and size output with ceil(ratio*frames).

**B4. [HIGH] iOS 17 phones collapse tabs 5–8 under a system More that collides with the app's own More tab**  
- *Why:* Confirmed ContentView.swift:148-179: legacyTabView emits 8 Tabs with no compact-width gating. On iPhone the classic UIKit TabView shows 5 items and pushes the rest (learn, phrases, stats, AND the app's .more) into the OS More list. Deployment target was just lowered to iOS 17 (commit 82130c4), so this is live for all iOS 17 users — a confusing double-More.  
- *Fix:* Cap iPhone to ≤5 primary tabs (Translate, Photo, Vocabulary, Learn, More) and fold History (already duplicated in More), Phrases, and Stats into More or their parent screens. Drive both compact and regular layouts from one AppTab source.

**B5. [MEDIUM] Screenshot stitching reads pixels with the wrong bytesPerRow, corrupting overlap detection**  
- *Why:* getPixelData renders into a context whose stride is 4*width (no padding) but findOverlapHeight indexes that buffer using the ORIGINAL CGImage's bytesPerRow (often padded to 16/32/64-byte alignment). Every row offset is wrong; the bounds guard then silently skips most comparisons, so overlap detection is effectively broken and stitched screenshots mis-join.  
- *Fix:* Return and use the same stride the buffer was allocated with (4*width) inside findOverlapHeight; never mix the source CGImage's bytesPerRow with a freshly-rendered 4*width buffer. Only scan the overlap strip rather than allocating full-image buffers for both images.

**B6. [MEDIUM] Vision OCR runs synchronously on the MainActor and silently drops images on non-vision providers**  
- *Why:* PhotoTextRecognitionService is @MainActor and calls handler.perform([request]) synchronously, so accurate-level OCR on a tall stitched screenshot blocks the main thread for seconds. Separately, cleanupRecognizedText/extractVocabulary pass imageData without checking provider.supportsVision; deepseek/minimax fall back to the text model and CloudAIService strips the image entirely, so vision tasks silently run text-only.  
- *Fix:* Make the Vision perform nonisolated/off-actor and hop back to MainActor only to publish results. Gate image paths on provider.supportsVision (reuse gradingProvider()); only pass imageData to chat() when the resolved provider actually supports vision.

**B7. [MEDIUM] CSV import corrupts any entry whose quoted field contains a newline**  
- *Why:* parseCSVImport pre-splits the whole file on newlines, but export quotes embedded newlines into a single multi-physical-line field. On re-import the splitter shreds that record, parseCSVLine sees unbalanced quotes, and the row is dropped or mangled — backup/restore is lossy for any multi-line definition.  
- *Fix:* Replace with an RFC 4180 state-machine parser that tracks quote state across physical line boundaries (accumulate until quotes balance). Add a golden round-trip test: export a term whose definition contains a newline/comma/quote, re-import, assert equality.

**B8. [MEDIUM] Spaced-repetition scheduling is structurally wrong and the correct code is dead**  
- *Why:* getCardsForReview/getDueCards (due-ordering + 20-card cap) have ZERO call sites; sessions are built by filteredStudyCards in raw deck order with no cap, so a 500-word deck becomes one 500-card session and 'Due for Review' shows due cards unordered. recordReview re-derives previousInterval from dates (collapses to ~1 day after a lapse, so intervals never grow), and quality 2 ('Difficult') is silently counted as INCORRECT. LearningCard.id is the Chinese string, so built-in and vocabulary cards collide in the progress dictionary and English-direction cards with empty Chinese all map to id=='', sharing one bucket.  
- *Fix:* Route reloadSessionCards through getCardsForReview(from:limit:). Persist a real interval/lapses on CardProgress (SM-2 style) instead of re-deriving from dates. Give cards a stable namespaced id ('builtin:<chinese>' / 'vocab:<SavedTerm.id>'). Decide explicitly whether 'Difficult' passes or lapses and make the thresholds agree.

**B9. [MEDIUM] Workbook grading and other power features are nearly undiscoverable**  
- *Why:* Confirmed: WorkbookGradingView is presented from exactly one place (PhotoTranslateView.swift:210) and has no top-level tab, no More entry, and no Shortcuts route. Camera scanner and screenshot translation are reachable only via App Intents; vocabulary import/export is macOS-only. A paid-vision-call feature that users will want to revisit is hidden, and grading results are lost on dismiss (no persistence).  
- *Fix:* Add a discoverable entry (primary/overflow action on Photo, plus a More hub row), persist gradings in a GradingHistoryStore (timestamp, score, questions, thumbnail) with a history list, and surface import/export on iOS. Add an onboarding tip pointing to Learn/Workbook.

**B10. [MEDIUM] Strict concurrency checking is off, so the audio data races compile clean**  
- *Why:* SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY is unset (Swift 5 mode) and Speech/AVFoundation are @preconcurrency-imported, so the genuinely off-actor buffer/converter/completion-handler races are never checked by the compiler — exactly the code where the use-after-free lives.  
- *Fix:* Set SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete on Debug, triage the warnings (they land on the audio tap/converter/continuation paths), then move toward Swift 6 mode. This converts the latent races into compile-time errors.

- **Save-to-vocab can store the wrong-language headword as the key, defeating dedupe and review** (workbook): The claim's central premise is factually wrong, and its proposed fix is already implemented.  1. correctAnswer is NOT the full-sentence field. The grading prompt (AIWordExplanationService.swift:968-976) defines TWO distinct JSON fields: "correctAnswer" = the answer to the question, and "fullSentence" = "the COMPLETE sentence... For a fill-in-the-blank, write the whole sentence with the correct word filled in." Complete sentences are deliberately routed to fullSentence, not correctAnswer. The GradedQuestion model confirms this: both are separate stored fields (lines 1310, 1315), and spokenSentence (lines 1335-1347) treats correctAnswer as a discrete answer word that is concatenated with the question text to build a sentence — it is not itself a sentence. So for the very "fill-in-the-blank" case the claim flags as common, correctAnswer is precisely the single missing word, which is the ideal vocab headword, not a sentence.  2. The fallback already prefers the model's vocab.term, exactly as the claim's proposed fix requests. vocabItem(for:) (WorkbookGradingView.swift:597-604) returns question.vocab whenever it has a non-empty trimmed term OR meaning (line 601), and only falls back to ExtractedVocabItem(term: question.correctAnswer, ...) (line 603) when the model supplied no usable vocab item at all. The claimed "fix" (prefer vocab.term) is the existing behavior.  3. The downstream harms (pinyin over a whole sentence, dedupe never matching) only materialize if premise #1 holds. Since correctAnswer is normally a short answer — and is only used as a last resort when even the model could not produce a vocab term — the realistic worst case is a short answer phrase, handled correctly by SavedTermsStore's normalizedKey dedupe (SavedTerm.swift:116-129, 185-188). - **Audio tap retains AVAudioPCMBuffer across async hop without copying — data race on reused buffer memory** (speech): The claim does not hold up. The cited code (SpeechRecognitionService.swift:440-446 and :458-485) does capture the tap-delivered `buffer` into an escaping `Task` that reads it asynchronously on the MainActor. However, the claim's foundational premise — that "AVAudioEngine ... its backing storage may be reused for subsequent taps" so reading it later is a data race / undefined behavior — is incorrect for AVAudioPCMBuffer.  Mechanism (independent analysis): 1. AVAudioPCMBuffer is a reference-counted Obj-C (NSObject) class that OWNS its sample storage via its AudioBufferList. Capturing it in the `Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) }` closure causes ARC to retain the buffer object; both the object and its owned `mData` audio memory stay alive and unmodified as long as that strong reference exists. AVAudioEngine allocates a fresh AVAudioPCMBuffer for each tap callback — it does not overwrite the mData of a buffer you have retained. So at line 467 (`buffer.frameLength`/`buffer.format.sampleRate`), in the converter pull-block at 473-476 (returning `buffer`), and at line 483 (`AnalyzerInput(buffer: bufferToSend)`), the buffer's samples are not subject to concurrent overwrite. There is no reused memory and therefore no data race on it. 2. Apple's own AVAudioNodeTapBlock documentation describes the block as receiving "copies of the output of an audio node" and carries NO "valid only for the duration of the block / must copy if retained" warning — unlike the explicit pool-reuse warnings Apple places on CMSampleBuffer from AVCaptureVideoDataOutput. The claim attributes CMSampleBuffer-style pool-recycle semantics to AVAudioEngine taps, which is not how this API behaves. 3. Retaining a tap buffer and processing it later via an async hand-off (continuation.yield / Task) is the conventional, Apple-sample-endorsed pattern for feeding SpeechAnalyzer; it would be broken if the buffer were unsafe to retain.  Note: there are unrelated latent concerns in this code (spawning an unordered Task per tap on the MainActor could reorder/drop audio chunks under load; the AVAudioConverter single-buffer pull-block is fragile), but none of those is the claimed defect. The specific claim — a data race / UB from reading reused/overwritten buffer backing storage — is not real and not reachable, because AVAudioPCMBuffer is reference-counted and the retained reference keeps the memory alive and stable. Verdict: invalid.
- **processAudioBuffer mutates AVAudioConverter from concurrent Tasks with no serialization** (concurrency): The claim's core mechanism is false. ModernSpeechEngine is @MainActor-isolated (SpeechRecognitionService.swift:360), and processAudioBuffer (lines 458-485) inherits that isolation, so all invocations serialize on the MainActor — there IS serialization, contradicting the claim's "no serialization" headline and "race" category (the claim even concedes "calls serialize on the actor"). Critically, processAudioBuffer contains NO await/suspension point: reading audioConverter (464), allocating convertedBuffer (465-468), and the synchronous converter.convert(...) call (473-476) all run as one atomic, non-suspending MainActor block before inputContinuation.yield (484). Because the actor serializes invocations and there is no interior suspension point, no second invocation can interleave with an in-flight conversion. The `buffer` captured by the inputBlock at line 475 is the per-call parameter of the currently-executing invocation (a local binding), not a shared field — so it can never return another task's "wrong/stale buffer." The alleged "concurrent use of AVAudioConverter" / "wrong buffer handed to converter" / "interleaved buffers" scenario is therefore impossible and unreachable. The only genuine residual concern is unrelated and much narrower: each tap spawns an unstructured Task { await self.processAudioBuffer(buffer) } (lines 443-445), and unstructured tasks have no guaranteed scheduling order, so 4096-frame buffers could occasionally be fed to the converter slightly out of capture order. That is a different defect from the one claimed, and its impact is low (minimal/inaudible resampling effects from rare reordering, no data corruption, no concurrent converter access). Defaulting to not-confirmed because the described defect does not hold up; adjusted severity to low to reflect the minor real residual ordering nuance.
- **WordTranslationService cache is mutated off the main actor without synchronization (data race)** (components): The claim's textual evidence is accurate (WordTranslationService at /Users/rogerlin/XCode-Projects/SwiftMandarinShortcuts/SwiftMandarin/Services/WordTranslationService.swift:14-22 is an @Observable final class, not source-annotated @MainActor, no Sendable, no lock; translationCache is read/written across await boundaries at lines 33-39, 49-55, 84-137; called from .task in RubyTextView.swift:438/444 and EnglishRubyTextView.swift:293). But the load-bearing premise — that this code runs off the main actor on a cooperative thread pool — is false for this project.  The Xcode project sets SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor for BOTH Debug and Release of the app target (project.pbxproj lines 352 and 425, under the target buildSettings with PRODUCT_NAME = $(TARGET_NAME)), together with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES. Under default-isolation=MainActor, every declaration lacking explicit isolation is implicitly @MainActor. I grepped all three cited files and found NO nonisolated, @concurrent, actor, Sendable, or explicit @MainActor annotations. Consequently WordTranslationService, its translationCache property, and all its async methods are implicitly @MainActor-isolated, as are fetchWordDetails(), translateWord(), and the enclosing .task closures.  An @MainActor async method runs on the main actor; it only suspends (off the actor) at the await on the underlying TranslationSession/AI call, then resumes on the main actor before writing translationCache. All cache reads/writes are therefore serialized on the single main actor. Two concurrent popovers or batch translation all execute on the main actor — there is no concurrent dictionary mutation, no data race, and no path to EXC_BAD_ACCESS from this code. The proposed fix (add @MainActor / convert to actor) is redundant because MainActor isolation is already applied module-wide via the build setting. The defect as described (an unsynchronized off-main-actor data race) is not reachable; marking invalid.
